evidence.text:
The platform supports attest collaboration only:

- auditor requests and responses (T1-04, T3-03);
- frozen audit populations and sample selections (T3-02);
- evidence delivery.

Our attest team works in-product as `Attest`-role engagement assignees,
behind the M0-D26 wall. External firms receive packages (M0-D17).

## Separation from management's records

The platform holds no attest workpaper, test conclusion, or report draft.
It may retain an issued report and the auditor-authored outcome as received in
the client's examination records (T1-07, T3-06); the product does not author or
recalculate the auditor's opinion. Management's evaluations and sign-offs
remain separate from that received outcome.
Auditor-identified exceptions are recorded as `AuditTestException`
(M0-D23), preserving the auditor's wording as received. They are not a test
workpaper.

## Retention on offboarding

Attest documentation lives in the attest team's audit software, under that
team's own retention obligations.

The client tenant holds only the collaboration records: requests, responses,
delivered evidence, and packages. Those follow M0-D16 retention and engagement
holds. No firm-level store is created (M0-D25).

Our attest team works in-product, so it has no delivered package by default.
To keep the record it relied on, closing an attest engagement, or offboarding
a client with an attest engagement, requires:

1. **Generate a record package.** An engagement record package in the M0-D17
   package format: every request, response, population and sample version,
   and delivered evidence item for the engagement, with its manifest.
2. **Record delivery.** An attributed decision records that the package was
   delivered into the attest team's audit software.

The engagement hold (M0-D16) blocks disposition until that delivery decision
exists, so offboarding (F1-01) cannot complete without it.

## Acknowledgement

- **Language:** the acknowledgement records that the person has read,
  understood, and agrees to comply with the exact policy version, identified
  by version and content hash. The text is a product default; an Org Admin
  may replace it per organization, and the acknowledgement stores the exact
  text shown.
- **Cadence:** new joiners have 30 days from their start date. Everyone else
  re-acknowledges annually, and whenever a new major policy version is
  approved.
- **States:** `pending`, `acknowledged`, `overdue`, `excepted`, or `removed`.

## Reminders

- **Members:** a pending acknowledgement for a workforce person who is a
  platform member follows the M0-D15 rules: in-app reminders, the weekly
  digest, and escalation at 7 days overdue.
- **Non-members:** a pending acknowledgement for a workforce person without a
  membership becomes a work item assigned to the campaign owner, who collects
  the acknowledgement and records it on the person's behalf. The same
  escalation applies. The product sends no email to non-members.

## Training

- A `TrainingRequirement` names the security-awareness course, the audience
  rule (same vocabulary as above), and the cadence: at hire within 30 days,
  then annually.
- The delivery source is `manual` or `lms_export`. A completion is a record
  with person, course, completed date and source, and the source artifact (an
  LMS export row or an uploaded certificate) is the evidence. An LMS connector
  is out of scope (M0-D20).

## Exceptions and joiner/mover/leaver

- **Exceptions:** an exception is a `Waiver` (M0-D23) with scope, approver
  (Compliance Lead), reason, and expiry of at most 12 months. Waived people

- Create a campaign from an exact approved policy or training requirement,
  frozen workforce population, applicable dates, owner, instructions, due date,
  and approved exceptions.
- Determine the audience from explicit rules and an accepted workforce snapshot;
  additions, departures, and role changes after launch remain explainable.
- Record delivery, acknowledgement, training assignment and completion,
  attestation, source, time, evidence, reminders, exceptions, and failed or
  missing delivery for each person.
- Accept reviewed completion records from an external LMS or manual evidence
  without pretending Compliance delivered the training content.
- Workforce people who never sign in remain eligible campaign participants.
  An authorized member records their externally collected acknowledgement or
  completion with the person, actual evidence, and entering-member attribution.
- Prevent a later policy or course version from satisfying an earlier campaign
  silently and prevent acknowledgement from proving comprehension or unrelated
  control operation.
- Route overdue, refused, failed, excused, and missing-source results into
  accountable work, review, and readiness.

Domain slice:

- Owns `PolicyDistributionCampaign`, `TrainingRequirement`, frozen audience,
  attributable acknowledgement, completion observation, reminder state,
  approved exception, and campaign result.
- Uses exact approved policy versions, workforce snapshots, responsibilities,
  source-aware completion evidence, and applicable control and criteria relationships.
- Produces reviewed communication and training evidence, gaps, audit
  populations, readiness effects, and stable engagement-snapshot records without
  becoming an LMS.

Acceptance criteria:

- The team can explain why every person was included, excluded, added, or removed from a campaign and which workforce snapshot supplied that decision.
- Each acknowledgement or completion identifies the exact policy or training version, person, source, time, and evidence.
- With no LMS export, connector, or optional automation enabled, the owner can
  maintain the audience, record an outside acknowledgement or completion and
  its support, review exceptions, and close the campaign through product actions.
- Missing delivery, overdue work, source failure, declined acknowledgement, and approved exceptions remain distinct and drillable.
- Policy supersession does not rewrite a launched or completed campaign and can deliberately trigger a successor campaign.
- Campaign totals reconcile to individually inspectable people and results and can supply a frozen audit population.

state.task: Select a concrete wire-compatible design for bounded Finding logical request receipts. User authorized making close decisions. Every new native business mutation must bind logical RequestId, actor and full normalized intent; exact older retries append nothing. Metadata ExecutionId is NOT logical RequestId.
state.existing: Seven current v1 Finding business contracts lack logical RequestId: FindingRaised/Revised, CorrectiveActionAdded/Completed, FindingAcceptanceLinked/Closed/Reopened. Original source fact JSON is hashed into migration lineage and Type I baseline content. Existing histories and their exact serialized business payload/hash must remain readable and stable; no fabricated request IDs for old records. JSON uses source-generated System.Text.Json; event metadata is a separate Portia envelope. Exact discriminator name/version resolves a registered CLR type; can retain exact legacy types.
state.scope: Only Finding facts/root, command handlers and directly required folds/source/projector consumers may change. Keep same canonical business names, no dual business emissions. New stream area findings already has native and imported v1 facts from local unreleased foundation; no verified production target usage. Legacy source programs remain fenced and imported one fact at a time. Commands use context.RequestId distinct from context.ExecutionId. Existing registered serializers include all seven v1 types.
state.additive: Option A adds optional init-only Uuid? RequestId to existing CLR/v1 contracts with JsonIgnore WhenWritingNull/default, so deserialized old records reserialize byte-for-byte with no added property. New native emitters must supply nonempty RequestId. Replay of old missing identities explicitly provides no retry proof. Aggregate methods require a command-selected identity for new mutations; import retains source payload unchanged. Preserve and test exact old fixture hashes. Advantage: small consumer change. Risk: same discriminator/version contains optional legacy and new receipt-bearing forms; correctness depends on fail-closed new-emission guards.
state.versioned: Option B defines explicit v2 canonical business contracts including required RequestId, retains renamed exact v1 CLR decoders/reducers and separate old-vs-new serialization branches/fold handling. Native commands emit only v2; imports retain exact v1 or v2 source kind/schema. Receipt handling is selected request only. Advantage: enforced schema distinction. Cost: seven compatibility types and all relevant serializer/migration/baseline/projector branches must support both, with exact legacy payload and lineage hash parity.

criteria.versioned_v2_exact_legacy: Use option B: explicit required-identity v2 facts and exact registered v1 compatibility CLR types; update all folds/migration/read/projector consumers with exact legacy lineage parity.

followUpJevDecisions.decision: A management response or Finding link may name any exact recorded received observation version, proved by fenced authoritative history; retain one selected historical proof rather than lifetime history in command state.

state.task: Settle one remaining concrete domain rule for received external auditor observations. User explicitly authorized selecting close choices. Existing selected owner AuditObservation keeps immutable received wording/versions separate from management responses and remediation Finding ownership. state.accepted: Decisions say each management response and Finding link names its exact received version; prior auditor wording and links remain retained. No existing product text says new responses/links must be limited to current received version. Corrections never rewrite prior versions. Backend issue301 supports machine-appropriate MCP for ordinary authorized management recording; actual personal signoff remains HTTP only.
state.current: Unreleased new root keeps scalar current received version, latest response/link and one command-selected receipt. Respond/Link currently reject any sourceVersion except current. New root has no registered command path yet. RaiseFinding currently accepts examination_item source without validation against exact received observation/version/wording. That authorized source seam must be fixed.
state.optionA: Require every new management response and Finding link against current received version only, with current source proof. Historical previously accepted responses/links and old exact retries remain immutable/readable. Simpler replay state. Cost: after auditor correction, management cannot newly answer or explicitly link remediation against the original received wording; they must reference current wording instead.
state.optionB: Allow new attributed response/Finding link against any exact actually recorded received version. A bounded root retains current state plus at most one command-selected historical source proof. An authoritative source-head-fenced history reader resolves and verifies original event/version/content hash/wording and all historical relationships; handler captures proof, not caller authority. Replay checks bounded local structure/scope/revision/source range and recorded proof; source history fold verifies exact received-content lineage without keeping lifetime history in command root. Each link/response explicitly names sourceVersion and immutable content hash. Wrong/future/unrecorded/forged source rejected. Cost: required history proof reader and consumer checks.
